recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34215; any future changes to Consent scope code status, history notes, or terminology publication should be handled in THO/UTG rather than in core source.
issue_request: FHIR-34215 was a Published/Persuasive CBCC change request asking to add `adr` back into the ConsentScope codelist because the R4 FHIR page showed four Consent scope codes while the terminology server CodeSystem `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/consentscope` showed only three, causing validation failures.
initial_application: No FHIR-core commit tagged with FHIR-34215 was found. Historical core source shows the local Consent scope CodeSystem was deleted by the UTG migration commit 5c0494aacf, and the practical application happened through the external UTG ticket UP-255, which was implemented and later published in THO 5.2.0.
additional_context: FHIR-31903 removed the `Consent.scope` element for R5 and merged scope-code usage into Consent category handling, so there is no current `Consent.scope` element binding to edit. The active Consent source folder still contains `valueset-consent-scope.xml`, whose source says the value set includes four Consent scope codes and includes the THO CodeSystem. Current THO JSON exposes `adr`, `research`, `patient-privacy`, and `treatment`.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing a core CodeSystem or hard-coding the concepts in the core value set would conflict with the UTG/THO ownership model; the current source plus current THO terminology already satisfies the issue.

related_jiras.note: UTG proposal that restored `adr` to `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/consentscope` and was published in THO 5.2.0.
R5 change that removed `Consent.scope`, explaining why there is no current Consent.scope element binding to edit.
